title: CrowdStrike Integrates Falcon Guardian Security into Amazon Bedrock and Claude Cowork

tickers.name: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The cybersecurity company has moved its AI Gateway tool into general availability, giving corporations a central interface to inspect prompts and enforce security policies for AI agents across managed and unmanaged devices. As part of an expansion of its Falcon Guardian suite, CrowdStrike also launched native security integrations for Amazon Bedrock and Anthropic's Claude Cowork, enabling enterprises to monitor autonomous agent activity and block prompt injection attacks without deploying separate software.

These product updates follow CrowdStrike's agreement to acquire security startups Fiddler AI and Dreadnode for a combined $495M in cash and stock. The acquisitions, which are expected to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, will add agent observability and automated vulnerability testing to the Falcon platform to detect hallucinations and behavioral drift in deployed AI models.

CrowdStrike is also scaling its cybersecurity presence through an expanded partnership with EY covering more than 20 member firms. Additionally, the firm introduced a new Falcon sensor for Amazon ECS Managed Instances to extend security coverage as containerized environments scale.

selectedTweets.text:
CROWDSTRIKE TO ACQUIRE TWO AI SECURITY STARTUPS FOR $495M

$CRWD has agreed to acquire Fiddler AI and Dreadnode as it expands its Falcon platform to secure AI agents throughout their lifecycle.

The acquisitions, include:

1) Fiddler AI (~$400M) | Agent Observability: Monitors AI agents, tracks their decisions and tool usage, and explains why they took certain actions. It can also identify hallucinations, behavioral drift and unintended actions.

2) Dreadnode (~$95M) | AI Security Testing: Tests AI models, applications and agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, using more than 100 attack strategies, including jailbreaks, prompt injection and agent-specific attacks.

The deals come as companies increasingly deploy autonomous AI agents with access to corporate systems, often faster than security teams can establish proper controls.

One major challenge is that an AI agent can have valid credentials and authorized access but still make incorrect decisions, ignore instructions or take unintended actions without being hacked.

Separately, CrowdStrike also introduced an AI Kill Switch within Falcon Guardian, allowing security teams to terminate misbehaving agents, prevent them from restarting and revoke their network access.

The feature is available through the AI Gateway today, with endpoint-level termination planned.

CrowdStrike plans to integrate Fiddler as Falcon Observe, while Dreadnode will add automated AI security testing to Falcon. Both capabilities are expected to become generally available in Q4 FY27.

The broader strategy is to bring AI security testing, agent monitoring and real-time intervention into a single platform, covering what agents are allowed to do, what they actually do and how to stop them when something goes wrong.

Both acquisitions are expected to close in Q4 FY27, with payments primarily in cash and some stock.
